reference: If both states sign the treaty, the border opens next month.
sk: Ak oba štáty podpíšu zmluvu, hranica sa budúci mesiac otvorí.
cz: Pokud oba státy podepíšou smlouvu, hranice se příští měsíc otevře.
acceptable: If {both|the two} {states|countries} sign the {treaty|agreement}, the border {will open|opens} next month.
If {both|the two} {states|countries} sign the {treaty|agreement}, next month the border {will open|opens}.
The border {will open|opens} next month if {both|the two} {states|countries} sign the {treaty|agreement}.

mistakes.text: If both states will sign the treaty, the border {will open|opens} next month.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „if“ patrí v First Conditional Present Simple: „if both states sign“, nie „will sign“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „if“ patří ve First Conditional Present Simple: „if both states sign“, ne „will sign“.
mistakes.feedback_en: In First Conditional use Present Simple after “if”: “if both states sign”.

mistakes.text: If both states signs the treaty, the border {will open|opens} next month.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Both states“ je množné číslo, preto sloveso bez -s: „sign“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Both states“ je množné číslo, proto sloveso bez -s: „sign“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “Both states” is plural, so the verb has no -s: “sign”.

mistakes.text: If both states sign the treaty, the border would open next month.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Ide o reálnu možnosť, preto „will open“; „would open“ patrí do Second Conditional.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Jde o reálnou možnost, proto „will open“; „would open“ patří do Second Conditional.
mistakes.feedback_en: This is a real possibility, so use “will open”; “would open” belongs to Second Conditional.

mistakes.text: If both states signed the treaty, the border {will open|opens} next month.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Pri reálnej budúcnosti patrí po „if“ Present Simple „sign“, nie Past Simple „signed“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: U reálné budoucnosti patří po „if“ Present Simple „sign“, ne Past Simple „signed“.
mistakes.feedback_en: For a real future situation use Present Simple “sign” after “if”, not “signed”.

mistakes.text: If both states sign the treaty, the border {will open|opens} in next month.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Pred „next month“ sa predložka nepoužíva: „opens next month“, nie „in next month“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Před „next month“ se předložka nepoužívá: „opens next month“, ne „in next month“.
mistakes.feedback_en: No preposition before “next month”: say “next month”, not “in next month”.

source_issues: Reference uses Present Simple “opens” in the result clause of a First Conditional exercise; Slovak and Czech use a perfective future, so “will open” is accepted too.
